text:
vikram: Heads up: hitting OOMs on 8xA100 runs with batch=48+KV cache warm. Profiling points to large transient NCCL comm buffers + ephemeral tempbuf spikes during TP all-gather. Link to nsys timeline: https://perf/reports/1970018753. Anyone seen transient buffer pinning issues recently?

anya: Yep saw something similar during the convo-run last week. My read: comm pool prealloc + KV cache shadow copies push us over workspace when kernels also allocate extra temporaries. What are your comm buffer reservation settings?

vikram: reserve_comm_bytes=1GB per-GPU, workspace_limit=40GB on an 80GB card. nvprof/nsys snippet shows repeated ~1.1-1.3GB allocations at ncclAllGather edges:

```
# nsys summary excerpt
Time  Event                Alloc (MB)
0.234 ncclAllGather_start  0
0.236 cudaMallocAsync       1150
0.238 ncclAllGather_copy   1150
0.240 cudaFreeAsync         1150
(repeats across shards)
```

Also seeing a burst when kernel selection flips to the int8 path for certain layers — temp workspace jumps.

jordan: A few levers we've used: lower comm pool watermark, enable comm buffer sharing, and force comm buffers into pooled staging arena instead of sticky staging. We landed `comm_buffer_sharing=true` in an internal flag last sprint. Can try `--comm-staging=pooled` for a quick experiment.

anya: Another gotcha: KV cache fallback previously made a shadow copy of shards when a fallback path triggered (so you briefly have two copies). There's a config `kvcache.shared_shards=true` in the branch that avoids the extra copy. If fallback path is happening often, that duplicates memory.

marie: FWIW I pushed a small change that reuses the NCCL ephemeral temp buffer between consecutive all-gather calls when seq_len distribution is stable. In my microbench it dropped peak transient by ~30% (and smoothed the alloc spikes). We haven't A/B'd at scale yet.

ops-bot: deploy job started for canary group 'nccl-temp-reuse' (job id 9872) by marie.

vikram: Nice. I'll run the canary with comm_watermark=512MB and `kvcache.shared_shards=true`. Attaching full nsys timeline and per-GPU alloc trace to the ticket. Also observed kernel selection toggling — cc @kevin to check quantization/kernel path heuristics.

kevin: On it. Kernel selection can switch heuristics when sequence length crosses internal thresholds. You can force the old path with `kernel.force=baseline` to see if temp demand drops. Also looking at whether the kernel chooser is allocating extra temp space for fused ops.

jordan: For immediate mitigation, reduce batch to 32 and enable prefix-KV compression (we have a small lossy compression option that reduces memory of cached prefixes). Ugly but buys time during the canary.

vikram: Plan: 1) roll marie's canary on a dedicated 8xA100 pool with lowered comm watermark; 2) patch kvcache fallback to avoid copy; 3) toggle kernel.force if canary still OOMs. Will report metrics (peak mem, OOM count, p95 latency) after run.

anya: If you see OOMs during canary, also collect `/proc/<pid>/maps` and the runtime allocator slab stats; they helped us pinpoint a staging arena leak earlier.

marie: Adding one more note: the reuse patch has a small risk when different NCCL collectives overlap — I added a guard to fail-safe to allocate separately in that case. We should include that guard in canary.

vikram: Thanks all. Starting canary now. If anyone can watch the canary GPUs for early OOM alerts that'd help (ping me in this thread). :crossed_fingers:

ops-bot: canary job 9872 started on pool 'canary-nccl-1' (8xA100). Logs available: https://ci/reports/9872

vikram: Will follow up with post-canary numbers and timeline screenshots.
